subject: Post-demo: QDX throughput probe plan and required artifacts
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@qdx.ai>, Bob Li <bob@qdx.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: QDX throughput probe plan and required artifacts

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible throughput/latency comparison against the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

What we saw today (high level)
- Redwood produced lower median latency on short prompts (<=128 tokens) and more consistent p95 for batched requests in our lab.
- You observed spikes on Hyperscaler-B at p99 for the long-sequence tests (1k+ tokens) — we want to reproduce that.

Goal for the probe run
- Recreate a tight A/B where we: Redwood hosted model variant vs Hyperscaler-B managed endpoint. Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, and CPU/GPU utilization. Capture cold-start and warm-cache behavior.

Proposed test matrix (short)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8
- Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024
- Workloads: QDX production prompt mix (you to provide), and our synthetic tails (attached)
- Metrics: tokens/sec, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), error rates, cost per 1M tokens

What we need from you
- Your representative prompt mix and token-length distribution (CSV is fine) — helps us pick percentiles to reproduce your tail.
- Permission to run 2x 2-hour windows against your Hyperscaler-B endpoints (non-prod) next week so we can collect comparable traces.

What Redwood will provide
- A test harness (redwood-probe-harness-v1.tar.gz) with workload driver and measurement scripts.
- Recording of today's demo and the exact probe payloads (demo-recording.mp4 attached).
- A short runbook explaining cache-warmup steps and how we toggle continuous batching.

Suggested schedule
- 2-hour slot Wed 4/11 10:00–12:00 PT (we can shift if that conflicts).

Next steps
1) Share your token distribution (Bob/Alice).
2) Marcus will set up the harness and exchange credentials for a temp test user.
3) We run the probe, collect traces, and share an A/B report (p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec).

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
[attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (video/mp4)]

From: Alice Chen <alice@qdx.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Li <bob@qdx.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QDX throughput probe plan and required artifacts

Thanks Priya — appreciated summary. Bob and I talked and we're onboard with the plan. A few clarifications before we schedule the slot: 

- We can open two non-prod endpoints on Hyperscaler-B for the probe but need to throttle to avoid impacting dev clusters. Is Redwood's harness able to respect client-side throttles?
- Attached is our token distribution export (qdx_token_distribution.csv). It skewed heavier than we expected in the 512–1k bucket.
- Can you share the exact request payload format your harness will use so we can validate no PII leaks?

Also — we prefer Thursday morning (4/12) for the run window if that works for your team.

Alice
Director, Platform Engineering, QDX AI
[attachment: qdx_token_distribution.csv (text/csv)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@qdx.ai>, Bob Li <bob@qdx.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QDX throughput probe plan and required artifacts

On Apr 9, 2028, at 3:02 PM, Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible throughput/latency comparison against the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Thanks — I'll own the lab run. Short notes from my side and a clearer matrix so Ops can sign off: 

Test harness notes
- The harness will do deterministic request pacing (tokens/sec target + poisson jitter) and record per-request timings. It supports client-side throttle config and respects a max RPS cap you set.
- We'll run each cell (batch x sequence length) for 15 minutes to get stable p99 estimates.
- Cache states: cold (fresh model instance), warm (KV cache primed with 10 representative prompts), and steady-state (continuous traffic for 20 minutes).

Requested inputs from QDX
- Confirmed non-prod endpoints and a short-lived API key (we'll delete keys after test).
- Your expected concurrency (typical RPS) and whether you use streaming responses.

Initial test matrix (detailed)
- Batch=1,4,8 x SeqLen=64,256,1024 x Cache={cold,warm,steady} x Runs=3
- Measurement: p50,p75,p90,p95,p99, tokens/sec, tail error codes, CPU/GPU pct

Artifacts we'll deliver after run
- Raw trace CSV, aggregated latency histograms, token throughput chart, and a short slide with interpretation and recommended knob changes (batching, kv-cache TTL, quantization recommendations).

Bob/Alice — if Thursday 4/12 10:00–12:00 PT works we'll provision the harness and share the Drive folder with scripts.

Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-probe-harness-v1.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@qdx.ai>, Bob Li <bob@qdx.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T18:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QDX throughput probe plan and required artifacts

Perfect — thanks Marcus and Alice. Quick consolidation and two action items so nothing slips: 

1) QDX (Bob) to drop the token distribution CSV and grant a short-lived API key for the non-prod Hyperscaler-B endpoints by Tue 4/11 EOD.
2) Marcus to upload harness to Drive and include runbook + exact request payload JSON by Wed 4/11 5pm PT.

We will run Thu 4/12 10:00–12:00 PT as agreed. After the run we'll produce an A/B report with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and a short set of ops recommendations for both Redwood and Hyperscaler-B setups.

I'll create a HubSpot task and calendar invite; HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-21987

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
